name: Cat-ear beanie

image.caption: Beanie with cat ears patterned as pride flags

lead: A cat-ear beanie is a knit hat with two pointed ears sewn on top. It is a style accessory rather than a grooming tool: it changes the silhouette of the head and signals a cute, soft or anime-inspired look.

It draws on nekomimi, the cat-ear motif from Japanese anime and manga, which has become a staple of cosplay, VTuber avatars and queer-youth fashion [1]. The e-boy aesthetic, popularized on TikTok in the late 2010s, favors a soft-boy look with layered clothes, chains and blush [2].

paras: Wearers pair it with oversized sweaters, chains, curtain-style bangs or pastel outfits, depending on the look they want. It is worn like any beanie and removed at will.
No health risks specific to the item are documented. Like any hat, it flattens hairstyles.

chain: Beanie with ears worn on head
angle.text: The beanie changes how the head and outfit read, adding a cute accent while worn. It is used for style rather than for any lasting change to appearance.

lead: A cat-ear beanie is a beanie with cat-shaped ears attached. People wear it to add a cute, playful accent to an outfit, with the visual effect lasting only while it is on.

The ears reflect nekomimi ('cat ears'), a Japanese anime and manga motif: cat ears became a regular youth accessory in 1980s Japan, and cat-eared characters are now common in cosplay and in VTuber avatars [1]. In Western online culture, queer and trans youth have adopted the catgirl or catboy image, with cat ears appearing in clothing such as pride-flag beanies [1].

The e-boy aesthetic, which emerged in the late 2010s and spread through TikTok, is described as drawing on emo, mall goth and scene fashion with a soft-boy presentation [2]. Typical elements are oversized sweaters, chains, curtain bangs and blush or winged eyeliner [2].

paras: The accessory combines an ordinary knit hat with sewn-on cat ears. Nekomimi refers to cat-like features on otherwise human characters, usually catgirls, with catboy as the male counterpart, within the wider kemonomimi category [1].

Catgirl imagery grew from Edo- and Shōwa-era cat-monster tales into approachable characters in works such as Princess Knight (1953) and Star of Cottonland (1978), and was common in anime and manga by the 1990s [1]. Cat ears are easy to add with minimal linework, which critics note helped the trope spread [1]. In 2024, four of the ten most-subscribed VTubers had animal ears [1].

The e-boy look, associated with TikTok and artists such as Lil Peep, is often presented as a soft-boy aesthetic [2]. Cat-ear headwear is part of the broader cat-ear fashion that queer youth and cosplayers have adopted [1].
